lines.text: **Unlike M18's group B, the B word here is usually not a qualifier.** In 81 verses *rule*, *dominion* or *authority* is itself the act read. The qualifier verses (47) are mostly proverbs. In them, who rules is only the setting or the outcome of another act: diligence (Pro 12:24), dealing wisely (Pro 17:2), the people rejoicing or groaning (Pro 29:2).

- **OT-98 (M18 × M72).** All 18 B verses among the 182 are decided here, on top of their M18 decisions. Judg 9:2, which the M47 register set as data (C), is read again for M72 (§2.3), because the B word carries it.
- 8 are read in §2 for the first time: Eph 6:12, Ecc 8:9, Judg 9:2, Act 8:19, Jude 8, Rom 13:1, Jer 51:46 and Jer 30:21.
- 4 go forward: Ecc 10:4, Act 5:4, Mar 1:27 and Luk 4:36.
- 4 are God's character (13.1): Mat 10:1, Mar 6:7, Joh 17:2 and Psa 103:22.
- 1 goes to the other spirits (13.3): Act 19:16.
**Psa 119:133, Rom 6:14.** The trial read these, and its readings stand.
**Psa 19:13.** *"Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me! Then I shall be blameless, and innocent of great transgression."*

- **The passage.** The verse before is *"Who can discern his errors? Declare me innocent from hidden faults"* (19:12). The verse after is *"Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight"* (19:14).
**1Cor 6:12.** *"'All things are lawful for me,' but not all things are helpful. 'All things are lawful for me,' but I will not be dominated by anything."*

- **The passage.** The verses after are about food and the stomach (6:13) and the body *"not meant for sexual immorality, but for the Lord"* (6:13). Then: *"your bodies are members of Christ"* (6:15).
- **Home:** Ch 11 §7, *what would rule within*. It points to 10.6 *Wanting that owns the one who wants* (Gen 4:7).

**Eph 6:12.** *"For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places."*

- **The passage, before:** *"Masters, do the same to them, and stop your threatening, knowing that he who is both their Master and yours is in heaven"* (6:9). Then *"be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might"* (6:10), and *"stand against the schemes of the devil"* (6:11).

- **The passage, after:** *"withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand firm"* (6:13). The armour follows: truth, righteousness, the readiness of the gospel of peace, and *"the shield of faith"* (6:14–16).

- **Pointer:** three verses earlier (6:9), a human master is told to stop threatening, *"knowing"* that he has a Master in heaven. In one passage, a master's rule over others is checked by the Master above him, and the believer stands against authorities above the human ones.
**Ecc 5:19.** *"Everyone also to whom God has given wealth and possessions and power to enjoy them, and to accept his lot and rejoice in his toil — this is the gift of God."*

- **Reading:** having goods is one thing. Having power over them, so that they can be enjoyed, is another, and the verse calls that power the gift of God. Ecc 6:2 (carried in 10.6) is the same case turned round: God gives the wealth *"yet God does not give him power to enjoy them, but a stranger enjoys them"*.

- **The person rules.** *"he who rules his spirit"* (Pro 16:32); *"you must rule over it"* (Gen 4:7); *"having his desire under control"* (1Cor 7:37); *"I will not be dominated by anything"* (1Cor 6:12).
- **God is asked to keep the person.** *"let no iniquity get dominion over me"* (Psa 119:133); *"let them not have dominion over me"* (Psa 19:13).
- **It is stated as a fact, under grace:** *"sin will have no dominion over you"* (Rom 6:14). Two verses earlier the same thing is a command: *"Let not sin therefore reign"* (6:12).
- **It is given or withheld by God:** the power to enjoy (Ecc 5:19; 6:2).
- **There is no power at all:** *"No man has power to retain the spirit"* (Ecc 8:8).
- **Something else is to rule:** *"Let the peace of Christ rule"* (Col 3:15).

- **I read:** where the thing that would rule is sin, the verses either ask God or speak of grace. Where it is a man's own spirit or desire, they say he rules it. Ecc 8:8 sets the outer limit: death and the spirit are not under any man's power.
- Lev 25:43 and Neh 5:15 (10.10 *The fear of God and the weak*)
- Isa 14:6 (10.10 *Anger between people*)
**1Pe 5:3.** The trial read it, and its reading stands (see below).
**The law's limit, given three times (Lev 25:43, 46, 53).**
- *"You shall not rule over him ruthlessly but shall fear your God"* (25:43).
- *"over your brothers the people of Israel you shall not rule, one over another ruthlessly"* (25:46).
- For an Israelite sold to a foreigner: *"He shall not rule ruthlessly over him in your sight"* (25:53).
- "fear" (M01) is what is set against it (25:43).

**Eze 34:4.** *"The weak you have not strengthened, the sick you have not healed, the injured you have not bound up, the strayed you have not brought back, the lost you have not sought, and with force and harshness you have ruled them."*

- **The passage.** *"Ah, shepherds of Israel who have been feeding yourselves! Should not shepherds feed the sheep?"* (34:2). *"You eat the fat, you clothe yourselves with the wool"* (34:3). *"So they were scattered, because there was no shepherd"* (34:5).
- "force" (M23) and "harshness" (M06 "severity", the word of Lev 25:43) are its manner.
- The result is stated as if there were no rulers at all: "because there was no shepherd" (34:5, 8). The rulers were there; the shepherding was not.

**Pro 28:15–16.** *"Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a poor people."* Next verse: *"A ruler who lacks understanding is a cruel oppressor, but he who hates unjust gain will prolong his days."*
**Ecc 8:9.** *"All this I observed while applying my heart to all that is done under the sun, when man had power over man to his hurt."*
- Two verses later he names what follows when evil is not checked: *"the heart of the children of man is fully set to do evil"* (8:11).
**2Sa 23:3.** *"The God of Israel has spoken; the Rock of Israel has said to me: When one rules justly over men, ruling in the fear of God,"*
- **Home:** 10.10 *The fear of God and the weak* (beside Lev 25:43). Ch 11 §7.
**Lordship turned round (Mat 20:25; Mar 10:42; Luk 22:25).**
- *"You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them. It shall not be so among you"* (Mat 20:25–26).
- Luke: *"The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and those in authority over them are called benefactors. But not so with you"* (Luk 22:25–26).
- Matthew and Mark: the request for the seats at his right and left, then the ten *"indignant at the two brothers"* (Mat 20:24).
- Luke: *"A dispute also arose among them, as to which of them was to be regarded as the greatest"* (22:24), at the last supper.
- In its place: *"let the greatest among you become as the youngest, and the leader as one who serves"*, and *"I am among you as the one who serves"* (Luk 22:26–27).
- The disciples' inner acts are wanting the first place, indignation, and dispute. 10.7 and 10.10 already carry these (Mat 20:21–22, 26, 27–28; Mar 10:44–45).
**1Pe 5:3** (trial) belongs to the same face. It names the motives of oversight: *"not under compulsion, but willingly … not for shameful gain, but eagerly"* (5:2).
**2Cor 1:24.** *"Not that we lord it over your faith, but we work with you for your joy, for you stand firm in your faith."*
- **The passage, before:** *"it was to spare you that I refrained from coming again to Corinth"* (1:23).
**1Cor 7:4.** *"For the wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband does. Likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife does."*

- **The passage.** *"Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by agreement for a limited time, that you may devote yourselves to prayer; but then come together again, so that Satan may not tempt you because of your lack of self-control"* (7:5).
- "self-control" (7:5) is what is at risk.
- The ground given is the lack of self-control that Satan can use (7:5). So mutual authority guards each one against what neither rules alone.
**1Ti 2:12.** *"I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; rather, she is to remain quiet."*

- **The passage, before:** men are to pray *"without anger or quarreling"* (2:8), and women to dress *"with modesty and self-control"* (2:9). *"Let a woman learn quietly with all submissiveness"* (2:11).
- **The passage, after:** two grounds, *"For Adam was formed first, then Eve; and Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and became a transgressor"* (2:13–14).
**Est 1:22.** He sent letters *"that every man be master in his own household and speak according to the language of his people."*

- **The passage.** Vashti refused to come (1:12; cited in 10.1, 10.13 and Ch 11). The counsel was that the noble women *"will say the same to all the king's officials, and there will be contempt and wrath in plenty"* (1:18). The decree was to have this result: *"all women will give honor to their husbands"* (1:20). *"This advice pleased the king"* (1:21).
- The motive given is fear of contempt and wrath (1:18), and the aim is honour (1:20). Honour, an inner act, is commanded by decree.
- **Pointer:** Dan 6:26 (§2.7), where a king decrees fear of God.
- **Home:** 10.10 *Ruling another*. Ch 11 §7. It points to 10.13 (1:12).
**Pro 22:7.** *"The rich rules over the poor, and the borrower is the slave of the lender."*
- Two verses later: *"Whoever has a bountiful eye will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor"* (22:9).

**Eph 6:9** (from §2.1, a passage verse with no B word): *"Masters, do the same to them, and stop your threatening, knowing that he who is both their Master and yours is in heaven, and that there is no partiality with him."*
- **Home:** 10.10 *Ruling another*, beside Lev 25:43.
- **The manner forbidden:** ruthlessly, harshly, with force (Lev 25; Eze 34:4); domineering (1Pe 5:3); lording it (Mat 20:25; 2Cor 1:24).
- the ruler's fear of God (Lev 25:43; 2Sa 23:3; Neh 5:15)
- brotherhood (Lev 25:46)
- the onlooker (Lev 25:53)
- the Master in heaven (Eph 6:9)
- the ruled belong to God (Lev 25:42, 55)
- **The inner ground of harsh rule:** feeding oneself (Eze 34:2), a lack of understanding and love of gain (Pro 28:16), anger (Isa 14:6).
- **Where rule comes from:** money and debt (Pro 22:7); royal decree (Est 1:22); mutual giving in marriage (1Cor 7:4).
- **Turned round:** greatness as service (Luk 22:26–27); working with others for their joy (2Cor 1:24); leading by example, willingly and eagerly (1Pe 5:2–3).
- Luk 4:6, the devil's offer of all authority (13.3)
- Dan 11:3–4, *"rule with great dominion and do as he wills"* (10.7 *Willing*)
- 2Pe 2:10, *"despise authority"* (Ch 7)
**Joseph's rule: hated, then received unawares (Gen 37:8; 42:6).**
- **Gen 37:8.** After the sheaves dream: *"Are you indeed to reign over us? Or are you indeed to rule over us?" So they hated him even more for his dreams and for his words.*

- **Gen 42:6.** *"Now Joseph was governor over the land … And Joseph's brothers came and bowed themselves before him with their faces to the ground."* Then: *"Joseph remembered the dreams that he had dreamed of them"* (42:9). *"Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him"* (42:8).
**Gideon refuses rule (Judg 8:22–23).**
- He asks for the earrings of the spoil (8:24).
- *"Gideon made an ephod of it … And all Israel whored after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his family"* (8:27).
**Abimelech seeks rule (Judg 9:2).**

- **The passage.** *"their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, 'He is our brother'"* (9:3). He hired *"worthless and reckless fellows"* with silver from the house of Baal-berith (9:4). He *"killed his brothers … seventy men, on one stone"* (9:5).

- Abimelech is the son of Jerubbaal, who is Gideon (Judg 6:32). The father had said "I will not rule over you". The son asks the men of Shechem to choose one ruler over seventy, and to remember that he is their flesh.
- **Face:** rule sought by appeal to kinship. It is the reverse of Lev 25:46, where brotherhood limits rule.
**Num 16:13.** *"Is it a small thing that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, that you must also make yourself a prince over us?"*

- **The passage.** Dathan and Abiram refuse twice: *"We will not come up"* (16:12, 14). Moses before this, to Korah: *"would you seek the priesthood also?"* (16:10). After: *"Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, 'Do not respect their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them'"* (16:15).
**Hos 8:4.** *"They made kings, but not through me. They set up princes, but I knew it not. With their silver and gold they made idols for their own destruction."*
- **The passage, before:** *"To me they cry, 'My God, we — Israel — know you'"* (8:2).
- The people say they know God (8:2). God says of their princes, "I knew it not".
**Act 8:19.** *"Give me this power also, so that anyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit."*
- **The passage.** *"he offered them money"* (8:18). Peter answers:
- *"you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!"* (8:20)
- *"your heart is not right before God"* (8:21)
- *"pray to the Lord that, if possible, the intent of your heart may be forgiven you"* (8:22)
- *"I see that you are in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity"* (8:23)
**Jude 8** (read with 2Pe 2:10, carried in Ch 7). *"Yet in like manner these people also, relying on their dreams, defile the flesh, reject authority, and blaspheme the glorious ones."*
- **Home:** Ch 7 (with 2Pe 2:10). Ch 12. 13.2 (Michael). Ch 11 §7, face *authority rejected*.

**Dan 5:16–17.** The king: *"you shall be clothed with purple … and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom."* Daniel: *"Let your gifts be for yourself, and give your rewards to another. Nevertheless, I will read the writing to the king and make known to him the interpretation."*
- **The passage.** At once Daniel recalls Nebuchadnezzar's greatness, given by God (5:18–19; in Ch 4, 10.7, 10.10), and his fall *"when his heart was lifted up"* (5:20).
- by the devil, for worship (Luk 4:6–7, carried in 13.3)
- Rule is **resented** (Joseph's brothers), **charged as self-made** (Dathan and Abiram), **set up without God** (Hos 8:4), and **rejected** (Jude 8).
**Already carried:** Rom 13:3 (10.12).
**Joh 19:10–11.** The trial read these, and its reading stands. Pilate claims his authority out of fear (19:8). Jesus names its source, *"given you from above"*.

**Rom 13:1–2.** *"Let every person be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been instituted by God. Therefore whoever resists the authorities resists what God has appointed"*.
- **The passage.** *"he is God's servant for your good"* (13:4). *"Therefore one must be in subjection, not only to avoid God's wrath but also for the sake of conscience"* (13:5; in Ch 8).
- **Home:** Ch 11 §7, face *where authority comes from*, beside Joh 19:11. Pointers to Ch 8 (13:5) and 10.12 (13:3).

**Tit 3:1–3.** *"Remind them to be submissive to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work, to speak evil of no one, to avoid quarreling, to be gentle, and to show perfect courtesy toward all people. For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, led astray, slaves to various passions and pleasures, passing our days in malice and envy, hated by others and hating one another."*
- The ground is given with "For": the memory of what we were ourselves (3:3), and *"the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior"* (3:4).
**The centurion (Mat 8:9; Luk 7:8).** *"For I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. And I say to one, 'Go,' and he goes"*.
- **The passage, Luke:** *"I am not worthy to have you come under my roof. Therefore I did not presume to come to you. But say the word"* (Luk 7:6–7; in 10.4).
- **The passage, Matthew:** *"When Jesus heard this, he marveled … with no one in Israel have I found such faith"* (Mat 8:10).
**The leaders' question (Mat 21:23–27; Mar 11:28–33; Luk 20:2–8).** *"By what authority are you doing these things, and who gave you this authority?"*

- *"And they discussed it among themselves, saying, 'If we say, From heaven, he will say to us, Why then did you not believe him? But if we say, From man, we are afraid of the crowd'"* (Mat 21:25–26).
- Luke: *"all the people will stone us to death"* (20:6).
- "fear" belongs to the passage: Mark has *"they were afraid of the people"* (11:32).
**Saul's authority (Act 9:14; 26:10, 12).**
- **Ananias:** *"here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on your name"* (9:14).
- *"I myself was convinced that I ought to do many things in opposing the name of Jesus of Nazareth"* (26:9)
- *"after receiving authority from the chief priests … I cast my vote against them"* (26:10)
- *"in raging fury against them I persecuted them"* (26:11)
- *"with the authority and commission of the chief priests"* (26:12)
- *"It is hard for you to kick against the goads"* (26:14)
- The characteristics are the conviction (26:9) and the raging fury (26:11). They carry no M72 word.
- Ananias, told to go to him, reasons from that authority to fear (9:13–14). The Lord answers with his own choosing: *"he is a chosen instrument of mine"* (9:15).
- *"Am I not free?"* (9:1)
- *"Do we not have the right to eat and drink? … to take along a believing wife … to refrain from working for a living?"* (9:4–6)
- *"Nevertheless, we have not made use of this right, but we endure anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ"* (9:12)
- *"I would rather die than have anyone deprive me of my ground for boasting"* (9:15)
- *"For if I do this of my own will, I have a reward"* (9:17)
- *"present the gospel free of charge, so as not to make full use of my right in the gospel"* (9:18)
- *"For though I am free from all, I have made myself a servant to all, that I might win more of them"* (9:19)
- He calls it *"my own will"* (9:17). Freedom and servitude are joined in one sentence: "free from all, I have made myself a servant to all".

**2Th 3:9.** *"It was not because we do not have that right, but to give you in ourselves an example to imitate."* Before it: *"with toil and labor we worked night and day, that we might not be a burden to any of you"* (3:8).
**1Cor 8:9.** *"But take care that this right of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak."*

- **The passage.** *"by your knowledge this weak person is destroyed, the brother for whom Christ died"* (8:11). *"if food makes my brother stumble, I will never eat meat"* (8:13). The weak conscience is in 8:7 (Ch 8).
- *"our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for destroying you"* (10:8). *"I do not want to appear to be frightening you with my letters"* (10:9).

- *"that when I come I may not have to be severe in my use of the authority that the Lord has given me for building up and not for tearing down"* (13:10). The verses before: *"we are glad when we are weak and you are strong. Your restoration is what we pray for"* (13:9).
- the gospel and those it might win (1Cor 9)
- an example to imitate (2Th 3:9)
- the weak brother (1Cor 8:9)
- building up, not tearing down (2Cor 13:10)
- **Pointer to R1:** in 1Cor 6:12 the danger of a right is that it rules its holder. In 1Cor 8–9 the danger is to another. **I read:** in both, the right is held loosely.
**Already carried:** Neh 9:37, *"They rule over our bodies and over our livestock as they please, and we are in great distress"* (10.7 *Willing*).
**Lev 26:17.** *"I will set my face against you, and you shall be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you shall rule over you, and you shall flee when none pursues you."*
- **The passage.** *"if you will not listen to me … if your soul abhors my rules"* (26:14–15). *"I will visit you with panic"* (26:16). *"I will break the pride of your power"* (26:19).
- The inner side follows in the same verse: fleeing *"when none pursues"*, after *"panic"* (26:16).
- *"he gave them into the hand of the nations, so that those who hated them ruled over them"* (Psa 106:41).
- *"Many times he delivered them, but they were rebellious in their purposes … Nevertheless, he looked upon their distress, when he heard their cry"* (106:43–44).

- *"But after they had rest they did evil again before you, and you abandoned them to the hand of their enemies, so that they had dominion over them. Yet when they turned and cried to you, you heard from heaven"* (Neh 9:28).
- **Home:** 10.9 (the cry under rule). 13.1 (hearing, delivering). It points to 10.7, which cites Psa 106:4–5 and 45.
**Lam 5:8.** *"Slaves rule over us; there is none to deliver us from their hand."*
- **The passage.** *"Our fathers sinned, and are no more; and we bear their iniquities"* (5:7). *"no respect is shown to the elders"* (5:12).
**Est 9:1.** *"on the very day when the enemies of the Jews hoped to gain the mastery over them, the reverse occurred: the Jews gained mastery over those who hated them."*
- **The passage.** *"the fear of them had fallen on all peoples"* (9:2). *"the fear of Mordecai had fallen on them"* (9:3; in 10.10).
**Judg 15:11.** *"Do you not know that the Philistines are rulers over us? What then is this that you have done to us?"*

- **The passage.** Samson answers, *"As they did to me, so have I done to them."* The men of Judah: *"We have come down to bind you, that we may give you into the hands of the Philistines"* (15:12). Then *"the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon him"* (15:14).
**Isa 63:19.** *"We have become like those over whom you have never ruled, like those who are not called by your name."*
**Hab 1:14.** *"You make mankind like the fish of the sea, like crawling things that have no ruler."*

- **The passage.** *"why do you idly look at traitors and remain silent when the wicked swallows up the man more righteous than he?"* (1:13). *"he sacrifices to his net and makes offerings to his dragnet"* (1:16). The Chaldeans are *"guilty men, whose own might is their god!"* (1:11).

**Jer 51:46.** *"Let not your heart faint, and be not fearful at the report heard in the land, when a report comes in one year and afterward a report in another year, and violence is in the land, and ruler is against ruler."*
- **The passage.** *"Remember the Lord from far away"* (51:50).
- Being ruled by others is named as **God's giving over** (Lev 26:17; Psa 106:41; Neh 9:28).
- It can be **accepted** (Judg 15:11) or **reversed** (Est 9:1).
- Its opposite is **God's own rule, longed for** (Isa 63:19).
- Daniel: *"it is you, O king, who have grown and become strong. Your greatness has grown and reaches to heaven, and your dominion to the ends of the earth"* (4:22).
- *"your kingdom shall be confirmed for you from the time that you know that Heaven rules"* (4:26).
- Daniel's counsel: *"break off your sins by practicing righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the oppressed"* (4:27).
- Twelve months later: *"Is not this great Babylon, which I have built by my mighty power as a royal residence and for the glory of my majesty?"* (4:30).
- *"While the words were still in the king's mouth, there fell a voice from heaven"* (4:31).
- Before giving the interpretation, Daniel *"was dismayed for a while, and his thoughts alarmed him"*, and he wishes the dream on the king's enemies (4:19).
- The king's rule is real and great (4:22). It is promised back to him on one condition: knowing that Heaven rules (4:26).
- The counsel tells him what that knowing would look like in a ruler: righteousness, and mercy to the oppressed (4:27).
- 10.1 or 10.12 for Daniel's alarm (4:19). Check when woven.
**Dan 6:26.** Darius: *"I make a decree, that in all my royal dominion people are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, for he is the living God"*.
- **The passage.** *"the king was exceedingly glad"* (6:23).
- Fear is ordered by law here, as honour is in Est 1:22.

- **The verses.** *"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness. And let them have dominion over the fish of the sea"* (1:26). *"And God blessed them. And God said to them, 'Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and have dominion'"* (1:28).

**Psa 8:4–6.** *"what is man that you are mindful of him … Yet you have made him a little lower than the heavenly beings and crowned him with glory and honor. You have given him dominion over the works of your hands"*.
- The psalm opens and closes with *"O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth!"* (8:9).
- He does not boast of the dominion. Set it beside Nebuchadnezzar's boast in Dan 4:30.

**Dan 2:37–38.** *"the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, and the might, and the glory, and into whose hand he has given, wherever they dwell, the children of man, the beasts of the field, and the birds of the heavens, making you rule over them all"*.
- The same king later says *"by my mighty power"* (4:30).
- 10.9 (the psalmist's wonder; Psa 8 is not yet cited)

**Luk 10:19–20.** *"Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall hurt you. Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven."*
- **The passage.** The seventy-two *"returned with joy"* (10:17). *"In that same hour he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit"* (10:21).
**Luk 12:5.** *"But I will warn you whom to fear: fear him who, after he has killed, has authority to cast into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear him!"*
- **The passage.** *"do not fear those who kill the body, and after that have nothing more that they can do"* (12:4). *"Fear not; you are of more value than many sparrows"* (12:7).
- **Home:** 10.12, beside Mat 10:28, the parallel already cited there twice.
**Hos 12:4.** *"He strove with the angel and prevailed; he wept and sought his favor. He met God at Bethel, and there God spoke with us"*.
- **The passage.** *"in his manhood he strove with God"* (12:3). *"So you, by the help of your God, return, hold fast to love and justice, and wait continually for your God"* (12:6).

findings.text: The verses: Daniel: *"it is you, O king, who have grown and become strong. Your greatness has grown and reaches to heaven, and your dominion to the ends of the earth"* (4:22).; *"your kingdom shall be confirmed for you from the time that you know that Heaven rules"* (4:26).; Daniel's counsel: *"break off your sins by practicing righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the oppressed"* (4:27).; Twelve months later: *"Is not this great Babylon, which I have built by my mighty power as a royal residence and for the glory of my majesty?"* (4:30).; *"While the words were still in the king's mouth, there fell a voice from heaven"* (4:31).; Before giving the interpretation, Daniel *"was dismayed for a while, and his thoughts alarmed him"*, and he wishes the dream on the king's enemies (4:19).

Reading: The king's rule is real and great (4:22). It is promised back to him on one condition: knowing that Heaven rules (4:26).; The counsel tells him what that knowing would look like in a ruler: righteousness, and mercy to the oppressed (4:27).; His boast claims the rule as his own power, and its glory as his own. The word comes "while the words were still in the king's mouth".
Home: Ch 12, or Ch 4 beside 5:20. 4:30 is not yet cited.; 10.10 (mercy to the oppressed as the ruler's remedy, 4:27).; 10.1 or 10.12 for Daniel's alarm (4:19). Check when woven.; Ch 11 §7.
The passage. *"the king was exceedingly glad"* (6:23).
Reading: A king who has seen God deliver decrees that his realm fear that God.; Fear is ordered by law here, as honour is in Est 1:22.
